chapters.screenText: Run your MATLAB workflow with native ISSM, then retain its results.
chapters.screenWhy: Bring your source, referenced data and native outputs into one reviewed workflow.
chapters.expectedResult: Use a verified BYO AWS connection, your MATLAB license and Connector.
chapters.title: 1. Run your own ISSM script
instructions: Goal: upload a small MATLAB workflow and a synthetic JSON input, run native ISSM on your connected AWS resources, then inspect and download its results.
Have an approved CryoStack login, a verified BYO AWS connection, and configured MATLAB plus Connector.
chapters.note: Open CryoLauncher. Choose Cloud → Advanced → ISSM.
chapters.why: Bring your source, referenced data and native outputs into one reviewed workflow.

chapters.screenText: Download the native tutorial packet and extract four input files.
chapters.screenWhy: The entry script, two helpers and JSON must be available before importing.
chapters.expectedResult: Scripts: runme.m, Launch.par, validate_launch_dataset.m; data: issm-shelf-small-v1.json.
chapters.title: 2. Download the tutorial inputs
instructions: Open Pilot Tutorials → Bring your own script and download the supplied native input packet. Extract it.

Scripts: runme.m, Launch.par, validate_launch_dataset.m.
Data: issm-shelf-small-v1.json.
chapters.note: Scripts are in examples/soft_launch/issm/. JSON is in examples/soft_launch/datasets/.
chapters.why: The entry script, two helpers and JSON must be available before importing.

chapters.screenText: Name your owned example, then choose New example.
chapters.screenWhy: An owned example gives your imported scripts a separate editable home.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep that example selected for scripts and dataset references.
chapters.title: 3. Create your workspace example
instructions: In Editor, enter a new name and choose New example.
This recording uses pilot-issm-script-1119. Keep the new owned example selected for the following uploads.
chapters.note: New ISSM examples include a starter runme.m. The supplied entry script replaces it.
chapters.why: An owned example gives your imported scripts a separate editable home.

chapters.screenText: Choose Upload to store the selected JSON dataset.
chapters.screenWhy: Uploading stores the selected JSON in your workspace dataset library.
chapters.title: 4. Choose Upload
instructions: One JSON file is selected. Choose Upload.
chapters.note: The next view keeps the actual action and confirmation.
chapters.why: Uploading stores the selected JSON in your workspace dataset library.

chapters.screenText: Read the uploaded filename and select it in the dataset list.
chapters.screenWhy: The filename confirms which dataset will be attached next.
chapters.expectedResult: The selected-file count changes from 1 to 0 when upload finishes.
chapters.title: 4. Confirm the JSON upload
instructions: The selected-file count changes from 1 to 0 when Upload finishes.
The confirmation names issm-shelf-small-v1.json. Keep this dataset for the next reference step.
chapters.note: Datasets are stored separately from source files.
chapters.why: The filename confirms which dataset will be attached next.

chapters.screenText: Choose Reference in example to attach the selected JSON.
chapters.screenWhy: A reference binds this dataset to the current owned example.
chapters.expectedResult: The next staged run will receive this dataset.
chapters.title: 5. Choose Reference in example
instructions: Select the JSON dataset, then choose Reference in example.
chapters.note: The next view keeps the actual action and confirmation.
chapters.why: A reference binds this dataset to the current owned example.

chapters.screenWhy: The exact relative path connects the attachment to the entry script.
chapters.expectedResult: This exact relative path is read by runme.m.
chapters.title: 5. Confirm the referenced filename
instructions: The confirmation gives data/issm-shelf-small-v1.json.
This is the exact relative path read by runme.m. The dataset is now referenced by this owned example.
chapters.note: The referenced bytes are copied into data/ when the next run is staged.
chapters.why: The exact relative path connects the attachment to the entry script.

chapters.screenText: Select all three scripts; enable Replace, then Import script files.
chapters.screenWhy: Replace is essential because a new ISSM example includes a starter runme.m.
chapters.expectedResult: Check count 0 → 3 → 0; replacement updates the starter runme.m.
chapters.title: 6. Replace and import all three scripts
instructions: Choose runme.m, Launch.par and validate_launch_dataset.m together.
Check Replace existing script files, then choose Import script files.
chapters.note: Watch selected count 0 → 3 → 0. Replacement is essential for the starter runme.m.
chapters.why: Replace is essential because a new ISSM example includes a starter runme.m.

chapters.screenText: Confirm all three filenames and Files are saved.
chapters.screenWhy: Check saved source before the next staging step snapshots it.
chapters.expectedResult: The accepted entry script is 37 lines; every submitted input hash matched.
chapters.title: 7. Confirm all three files are saved
instructions: Read the confirmation: runme.m, Launch.par and validate_launch_dataset.m are imported and Files are saved.
The entry script now shows 37 lines, saved.
chapters.note: All three scripts and the referenced JSON matched the expected hashes before launch and in the submitted snapshot.
chapters.why: Check saved source before the next staging step snapshots it.

chapters.screenText: Confirm Action Run and Run target runme.m.
chapters.screenWhy: The entrypoint chooses which MATLAB workflow is actually executed.
chapters.expectedResult: Launch.par, the validator and referenced JSON accompany the entrypoint.
chapters.title: 8. Confirm the entrypoint
instructions: In Experiment, set Action to Run and Run target to runme.m.
Keep the owned example and the three saved scripts from the previous steps.
chapters.note: The selected entry script is runme.m; the two helpers and referenced JSON accompany it.
chapters.why: The entrypoint chooses which MATLAB workflow is actually executed.

chapters.screenText: Review the owned ISSM run, then launch from the bottom of the review.
chapters.screenWhy: The normal review checks resources, license and the selected example.
chapters.expectedResult: Check the model, example, resources, configured license and Connector.
chapters.title: 9. Review the run
instructions: Choose Review & Launch. Confirm model ISSM, your owned example, and the resources shown in the review.
Use the existing configured license and Connector. Scroll to the bottom and choose Launch cloud run.
chapters.note: This native run used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB. The task time limit was 60 minutes.
chapters.why: The normal review checks resources, license and the selected example.

chapters.screenText: Follow the new submission until Completed.
chapters.screenWhy: Follow the new submission rather than a previous completed run.
chapters.expectedResult: Wait for this run’s results, rather than a previous completed run.
chapters.title: 10. Follow the new submission
instructions: The new run enters Submitting, then Queued while AWS starts the container.
Wait for Running and Completed before opening its results.
chapters.note: The launch confirmation precedes this actual new submission.
chapters.why: Follow the new submission rather than a previous completed run.

chapters.screenText: Check completion before opening the native results.
chapters.screenWhy: Startup, task time and script time describe different intervals.
chapters.expectedResult: Startup 219.980 s; Batch task 45.010 s; script interval 2.156 s.
chapters.title: 11. Completion and elapsed times
instructions: The native run completed successfully.

Submission → Batch start: 219.980 s.
Batch task: 45.010 s.
Script-reported interval: 2.156046 s.
chapters.note: Startup, task time and script time measure different intervals.
chapters.why: Startup, task time and script time describe different intervals.

chapters.screenWhy: Render displays the selected native result without rerunning the solve.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: one diagnostic solution with 13 native nodal values.
chapters.title: 12. Render the native velocity
instructions: In Workspace → Results, choose StressbalanceSolution and Vel, then choose Render.
This is the recorded Render action and its native output.
chapters.note: The selected output contains one diagnostic solution and 13 nodal values.
chapters.why: Render displays the selected native result without rerunning the solve.

chapters.screenText: Inspect the saved native velocity figure and its units.
chapters.screenWhy: Use the figure, mesh count and node-weighted metric together.
chapters.title: 13. Inspect the saved native field
instructions: The unchanged native PNG shows speed in metres/year.
13 vertices and 16 triangles. Speed ranges from 0 to 18.89046 m/year.
Node-RMS speed is 6.2386984 m/year. Convergence is the scalar 25.
chapters.note: The 10 km square uses one diagnostic SSA Stressbalance solve, without physical time advance.
chapters.why: Use the figure, mesh count and node-weighted metric together.

chapters.screenText: Choose Download results, then save the fresh archive link.
chapters.screenWhy: Retain the native fields with source/data hashes and runtime provenance.
chapters.expectedResult: Retain the 13-member result ZIP with the input and runtime manifests.
chapters.title: 14. Download this run’s results
instructions: Choose Download results, then use the fresh HTTPS download link.
The saved ZIP has 13 CRC-valid members: mesh, native fields and figure, model, metrics and runtime/RNG provenance.
chapters.note: Keep the archive together with the input manifest and recorded runtime versions.
chapters.why: Retain the native fields with source/data hashes and runtime provenance.

chapters.screenText: Interpret the script’s actual initial and boundary conditions.
chapters.screenWhy: The actual script and boundary conditions define this diagnostic result.
chapters.expectedResult: Zero initial and constrained-boundary velocity; the JSON speed is unused.
chapters.title: 15. What this example establishes
instructions: This script starts with zero velocity and fixes its non-front boundary velocities. The shared JSON speed setting is unused.
Thickness is source-confirmed at 300–500 m; its arithmetic-node mean is 400 m. The saved model geometry is opaque locally.
chapters.note: One verified native diagnostic execution. Full source/data/runtime receipts are linked; this is not a repeat or accuracy result.
chapters.why: The actual script and boundary conditions define this diagnostic result.
